update.title: Built a real-time webcam background removal pipeline
update.summary: Built a real-time webcam pipeline that used Robust Video Matting to separate the foreground, replace or blur the background, and expose the result as a standard V4L2 camera.
update.previewAlt: RVM composited output placing a person against a solid blue virtual background

blocks.body:
## Turn background removal into an ordinary camera

I built RVM Virtual Camera so real-time background removal could work in applications that knew nothing about the model behind it. The program opened a physical webcam, passed each frame through a Robust Video Matting model loaded with PyTorch, composited the foreground, and wrote the finished frame to a V4L2 loopback device.

OBS, conferencing tools, and browser calls could select that output like an ordinary camera.

blocks.caption: The machine-learning pipeline terminated at a standard virtual-camera boundary, keeping consumers independent of the model.
blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  Camera[Physical webcam] --> Capture[Threaded frame capture]
  Capture --> RVM[Robust Video Matting model]
  RVM --> Matte[Foreground and alpha matte]
  Background[Solid color, image, or blurred frame] --> Composite[Frame composition]
  Matte --> Composite
  Composite --> Preview[Optional preview]
  Composite --> V4L2[V4L2 loopback camera]
  V4L2 --> Calls[OBS, browser, or call application]
blocks.summary: The machine-learning pipeline terminated at a standard virtual-camera boundary, keeping consumers independent of the model.

blocks.body:
## Keep the frame loop practical

Capture ran on its own thread, keeping camera reads separate from inference and the optional preview. Explicit resolution, frame rate, and downsample controls provided a practical way to balance image quality and throughput. The lighter MobileNetV3 model and heavier ResNet50 model offered another performance choice based on available GPU capacity.

The pipeline could place the subject over a solid color or chosen image, or blur the original background while preserving the foreground. The preview combined the source frame, composited result, and alpha matte side by side so each stage could be checked before another application consumed the virtual camera.

blocks.body:
## Make the host boundary explicit

Camera input, processed output device, optional raw passthrough device, model, resolution, frame rate, background mode, and downsample ratio were command-line options rather than hardcoded to one workstation. The output still depended on a loaded `v4l2loopback` device, while CUDA and half-precision inference made the model substantially more practical at interactive frame rates.
